Subject: Private deployment: local snapshot access & operator SLA negotiation

Hi Alyssa / Kyle —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. As promised, attaching our redlines to the MSA + Order Form focused on the private (on-prem / VPC) deployment exhibits. High level items we think need resolution to proceed to procurement:

- license/ownership boundary for locally-hosted snapshots (Exhibit B) — we proposed read-only snapshot access for the customer with a documented witness process rather than direct operator keys being handed over
- operator SLA and hot-swap commitments — proposed 4 hour failover window in operational annex
- scope of audit & evidence requests — we flagged a path for staged artifacts to satisfy SOC-like evidence without full code escrow
- encryption & key custody options — suggested KMS-backed escrow or third-party custodian for key handoffs

Attachments: MSA_OrderForm_v5_redlines.pdf, proposed-operator-sla-draft.docx

Can you review the redlines and let us know which of the above is a hard stop for Nova? If possible, we'd like to slot a 30-minute legal + procurement call early next week with Aditya on the pricing/commit impact of any changes.

Proposed times (PST): Mon 6/21 10:00 or Tue 6/22 11:00.

Cheers,
Mina Haddad
Senior Sales Operations, Redwood Inference

Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment: local snapshot access & operator SLA negotiation

Mina —

Thanks for the detailed packet. Quick reactions from legal/procurement:

- Local snapshot access: we cannot accept language that grants Nova unfettered local access to the operator key material or the ability to run arbitrary maintenance workflows. Our preference is for a witnessed transfer model where a neutral custodian or a mutually agreed third party encrypts the snapshot and witnesses the handover.

- Operator SLA: procurement is sympathetic to a hot-swap commitment, but 4 hours is aggressive for our internal change controls. Would you consider a 12-hour window with staged penalties? We need to understand how that maps to the Dedicated vs Private pricing tiers.

- Audit evidence: we can accept staged artifacts (runbooks, test access logs) but we need a narrower evidence scope limited to operational readiness items rather than any developer access.

I've attached our counterproposal comments inline in the MSA (NOVA_counterproposal_MSA_notes.pdf). Legal flagged specific wording in Exhibit B (definition of "snapshot" and "operator credentials") that we should redline together.

Let's take the call — Mon 6/21 10:00 PST works for Kyle and me. Please share a dial-in or calendar invite.

Best,
Alyssa Green
General Counsel, Nova Clinic
[Attachment: NOVA_counterproposal_MSA_notes.pdf (pdf)]

Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 15:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment: local snapshot access & operator SLA negotiation

Alyssa —

Appreciate the quick read — useful notes. Short responses and a proposed middle path to present on the call:

1) Snapshot custody: agree that handing over operator keys is not acceptable. Proposed compromise: time-limited, encrypted snapshot export that is produced by Redwood on an audited run, encrypted to a customer-provided public key and uploaded to a mutually-controlled S3 location. A neutral witness (third-party custodian or Nova's infosec witness) signs off on the export event; we will retain detailed run logs and an audit hash chain.

2) Witnessing vs escrow: if Nova is comfortable with the above, we can avoid a full code escrow. If Nova insists on an escrow-like assurance, we recommend KMS-based split-key escrow with a trusted custodian. We can draft both options as Exhibit B alternatives.

3) SLA window: Aditya asked me to surface cost delta for different hot-swap targets. If we agree to 12 hours with a 6-hour escalation (i.e., target 6, contractual 12) we can propose a middle-tier pricing uplift instead of the highest Dedicated commitment. Aditya, can you confirm rough % uplift ranges?

4) Evidence scope: we propose a checklist (runbook, witness attestation form, sample logs, restore DR test report) rather than unfettered access. I'll circulate a short checklist before the call.

Call confirmed: Mon 6/21 10:00 PST. I've added Aditya to keep pricing impacts in the room.

Thanks —
Mina
Senior Sales Ops, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: proposed-operator-sla-draft.docx (docx)]

Team —

Quick summary after today's notes and the call agenda:

- Agreement in principle: neutral-witnessed encrypted snapshot export OR KMS split-key escrow as Exhibit B alternatives. Alyssa to confirm preferred path by EOD Thu 6/24.
- SLA: tentative compromise of operational target 6 hours, contractual 12 hours; procurement to confirm pricing uplift. Aditya to provide uplifts and a one-page impact table by Wed 6/23.
- Evidence checklist: Mina will circulate the 6-item checklist (runbook, witness attestation template, sample logs, restore test, console audit sample, operator onboarding checklist) by EOD 6/22.
- Contract edits: legal teams to focus on tightening the definition of "operator credentials" and adding explicit read-only language for customer snapshot artifacts.

Attachments: mutual-action-plan.xlsx (simple MLP with owners/dates). I'll own the follow-up to close the language on Exhibit B.

Connor O'Brien
